examples.en: I watched the movie in high-definition video.
This camera shoots in high quality.
It is high-definition, so the face is clear.
To watch high quality, your internet has to be fast.
High-resolution photos have large files.
High quality is nice, but I worry about the storage.

explain: 반대말은 '저화질'이에요. 일상에서는 '화질이 좋아요', '화질이 안 좋아요'처럼 말하기도 해요.

phrases.en: Please send a high-quality photo.
phrases.nuance_ko: '고화질' 뒤에 사진이나 영상 같은 말을 붙여 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Put words like photo or video after 고화질.

phrases.en: This phone has good picture quality.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상 대화에서 더 자주 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A more common way to say it in daily conversation.

phrases.en: Low-quality video is hard to see.
phrases.nuance_ko: '고화질'의 반대말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The opposite of 고화질.

explain_en: The opposite is 'jeohwajil'. In daily talk people also say 'hwajiri joayo' (the picture quality is good) or 'hwajiri an joayo'.

examples.en: This song has really beautiful lyrics.
We memorized the lyrics and sang together.
I heard the singer wrote the lyrics herself.
I looked up the words in the lyrics in the dictionary.
I like both the lyrics and the melody.
To study Korean, I learn words through song lyrics.

explain: '가사'와 같은 뜻으로 써요. 노랫말은 우리말 단어이고 가사는 한자어예요. '가사'는 집안일이라는 뜻도 있어서 헷갈릴 때 '노랫말'이라고 하면 분명해요. '노랫말을 쓰다'처럼 써요.

phrases.en: This song has good lyrics.
phrases.nuance_ko: 노랫말과 같은 뜻이지만 한자어예요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as 노랫말, but it's a Sino-Korean word.

phrases.en: My friend wrote the lyrics himself.
phrases.nuance_ko: 노래의 글을 직접 만들 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use this for creating the words of a song.

phrases.en: The lyrics were sad, so I cried.
phrases.nuance_ko: 노랫말의 느낌을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use this to describe how the lyrics feel.

explain_en: It means the same as '가사'. 노랫말 is a native Korean word while '가사' is Sino-Korean. '가사' also means housework, so saying 노랫말 makes it clear. You say '노랫말을 쓰다'.

examples.en: Please draw a rhombus on the board.
This shape is not a square but a rhombus.
A baseball infield is shaped like a diamond.
I folded the paper and cut it into a diamond shape.
How are a rhombus and a square different?

examples.ko: 아이가 마름모 무늬 옷을 입고 있어요.
examples.en: The child is wearing clothes with a diamond pattern.

explain: 수학 시간에 '정사각형', '직사각형', '사다리꼴'과 함께 도형 이름으로 배워요. 일상에서는 '다이아몬드 모양'이라고도 말해요. 모양을 말할 때는 '마름모꼴'도 써요.

phrases.en: This window is diamond-shaped.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-꼴'은 모양을 뜻해서 마름모 모양을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: -꼴 means shape, so this describes a rhombus shape.

phrases.en: A square and a rhombus look similar.
phrases.nuance_ko: 수학 시간에 다른 도형과 함께 비교해서 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when comparing it with another shape in math class.

phrases.en: I drew a rhombus in my notebook.
phrases.nuance_ko: '그리다'와 함께 도형을 그릴 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: With 그리다 to talk about drawing the shape.

explain_en: You learn it in math class together with '정사각형', '직사각형' and '사다리꼴' as a shape name. In daily life people also say '다이아몬드 모양'. For the shape itself you can also say '마름모꼴'.

examples.en: That person has really good manners.
Table manners differ a little from country to country.
You have to mind your manners in public places.
Let's learn subway manners too.

examples.ko: 저는 첫인사 매너에 신경을 많이 써요.
examples.en: I pay a lot of attention to manners when greeting someone.
I judge people by their manners, not their looks.

explain: '매너가 좋다', '매너가 없다'처럼 써요. '매너'는 외래어라서 가볍게 말할 때 어울리고, '예의'는 더 정중한 한자어예요. '예의 바르다'와 '매너 좋다'처럼 같이 쓰는 말도 달라요.

phrases.example: 줄을 안 서는 건 매너가 없는 행동이에요.
phrases.en: Not standing in line is bad manners.
phrases.nuance_ko: 예의 없이 행동하는 것을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say someone behaves without courtesy.

phrases.en: You should keep good manners in a theater.
phrases.nuance_ko: 규칙처럼 지켜야 하는 행동을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for behavior one should follow like a rule.

phrases.en: I show respect to elders.
phrases.nuance_ko: '매너'보다 정중한 한자어예요.
phrases.nuance_en: A more formal Sino-Korean word than 'manner'.

explain_en: It is used as '매너가 좋다' or '매너가 없다'. '매너' is a loanword that suits casual speech, while '예의' is a more formal Sino-Korean word. They also pair with different words: '예의 바르다' versus '매너 좋다'.

examples.ko: 약속을 해 놓고 연락도 없이 안 오다니, 정말 무책임해요.
examples.en: Making a promise and not showing up without a word is really irresponsible.

examples.ko: 담당자가 무책임한 탓에 문제가 더 커졌어요.
examples.en: The problem got bigger because the person in charge was irresponsible.
Don't talk irresponsibly; take responsibility to the end.

examples.ko: 그 사장님은 직원들에게 무책임하다는 말을 들었어요.
examples.en: That boss was told by his staff that he was irresponsible.
If you take on a job and just leave, that's irresponsible.

examples.ko: 제가 무책임했던 것 같아요. 정말 죄송해요.
examples.en: I think I was irresponsible. I'm really sorry.

explain: 반대는 '책임감이 있다', '책임감이 강하다'예요. 명사 '무책임'은 '무책임 그 자체'처럼 쓰기도 해요. 상대를 강하게 비난하는 말이라서 직접 말할 때는 조심해요.

phrases.example: 무책임한 행동은 다른 사람에게 피해를 줘요.
phrases.en: Irresponsible behavior causes harm to others.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-ㄴ'을 붙여 뒤에 오는 명사를 꾸며요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding '-ㄴ' lets it describe the noun that follows.

phrases.en: You look irresponsible for not turning in the homework.
phrases.nuance_ko: 겉으로 그렇게 보인다고 조금 부드럽게 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Says someone seems irresponsible, a bit more gently.

phrases.en: That person has no sense of responsibility.
phrases.nuance_ko: '무책임하다'와 비슷하지만 조금 더 부드러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar to '무책임하다' but a little softer.

explain_en: The opposite is '책임감이 있다' or '책임감이 강하다'. The noun '무책임' can be used as in '무책임 그 자체' (irresponsibility itself). It strongly criticizes the other person, so be careful using it directly.

examples.en: I read an English email using a translator.
The translator sometimes translates strangely.
A translator is enough for short sentences.
I installed a new translation app.
I will try speaking Korean without a translator.
I pasted the sentence into the translator.

explain: 사람이 아니라 프로그램이 번역하는 것이에요. 사람이 번역하는 직업은 '번역가'라고 해요. '번역기를 돌리다'라고도 말해요.

phrases.en: I run a translator on sentences I don't know.
phrases.nuance_ko: 번역 프로그램을 실행해서 쓴다는 일상적인 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A casual way to say you run a translation program.

phrases.en: I read the menu with a translation app.
phrases.nuance_ko: 휴대폰으로 쓰는 번역 프로그램을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it for a translator on a phone.

phrases.en: The translator's result is a bit strange.
phrases.nuance_ko: 번역기가 만든 문장을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it for the sentence the translator produced.

explain_en: It is a program doing the translation, not a person. A person who translates as a job is a '번역가'. People also say '번역기를 돌리다'.

examples.en: The photographer took a nice family photo for us.
We hired one photographer for the wedding.
I have an uncle who works as a photographer.

examples.ko: 사진사에게 여권 사진을 찍어 달라고 했어요.
examples.en: I asked the photographer to take my passport photo.

examples.ko: 저 사진사는 아이들을 잘 웃게 해요.
examples.en: That photographer is good at making children laugh.

examples.ko: 졸업식 날 사진사와 같이 운동장을 돌아다녔어요.
examples.en: On graduation day I walked around the field with the photographer.

explain: '사진작가'는 작품을 만드는 느낌이 강하고, '사진사'는 사진관이나 행사에서 찍어 주는 사람에게 어울려요. 영상을 찍는 사람은 '카메라맨'이라고 해서 달라요.

phrases.example: 사진사님, 한 장만 더 찍어 주세요.
phrases.en: Mr. photographer, please take one more picture.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사진사를 직접 부르거나 높여 말할 때 '-님'을 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add '-님' when you address or speak politely about a photographer.

phrases.en: I want to become a photographer later.
phrases.nuance_ko: 꿈이나 직업을 이야기할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use this to talk about dreams or jobs.

phrases.en: I asked the photographer to take the family photo.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사진을 대신 찍어 달라고 할 때 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use this when you ask someone to take photos for you.

explain_en: '사진작가' feels like someone making artwork, while '사진사' fits a person who takes photos at a studio or an event. A person who shoots video is a '카메라맨', which is different.

examples.en: This problem seems very hard to me.
At first that job seemed easy to me.

examples.ko: 오늘은 비가 올 것 같다고 생각돼서 우산을 챙겼어요.
examples.en: I thought it might rain today, so I packed an umbrella.

examples.ko: 이 방법이 가장 좋다고 생각되는 이유가 있어요.
examples.en: There is a reason this method seems best to me.

examples.ko: 다음 주에는 모든 게 달라질 거라고 생각되지 않아요.
examples.en: I don't think everything will change next week.
If it seems that way to you, please tell me honestly.

explain: '생각하다'는 내가 생각을 만드는 것이고, '생각되다'는 그렇게 느껴진다는 부드러운 표현이에요. 발표나 보고서에서 의견을 조심스럽게 말할 때 '-다고 생각돼요/생각됩니다'를 자주 써요. '생각나다'(떠오르다)와는 달라요.

phrases.en: I think more study time is needed.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-다고 생각되다'로 의견을 부드럽게 말해요. 발표나 글에서 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use -다고 생각되다 to state an opinion softly; common in presentations and writing.

phrases.example: 저는 그 말이 맞다고 생각되지 않아요.
phrases.en: I don't think that statement is right.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-지 않다'를 붙여 부드럽게 반대 의견을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add -지 않다 to politely disagree.

phrases.en: That method seems to be wrong.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-(으)로 생각되다'로 그렇게 여겨진다고 조심스럽게 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use -(으)로 생각되다 to say carefully that something is considered a certain way.

explain_en: '생각하다' is you forming a thought; '생각되다' is a softer way to say it comes across that way. In presentations and reports, '-다고 생각돼요/생각됩니다' is common for stating an opinion carefully. It is different from '생각나다' (to come to mind).

examples.en: We learned about the Roman Empire in world history class.

examples.ko: 저는 세계사에 관심이 많아서 책을 많이 읽어요.
examples.en: I am very interested in world history, so I read many books.
World history is hard because there is a lot to memorize.
I study Korean history and world history together.

examples.ko: 이 시험은 세계사에서 문제가 많이 나와요.
examples.en: This test has many questions from world history.
I want to learn world history too.

explain: 학교에서는 '한국사'와 따로 배우는 과목 이름이기도 해요. 그래서 '한국사와 세계사'처럼 둘을 같이 말하는 때가 많아요.

phrases.en: I study Korean history and world history together.
phrases.nuance_ko: 학교 과목을 말할 때 두 과목을 같이 묶어서 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to name the two school subjects together.

phrases.en: I learned world history in high school.
phrases.nuance_ko: 과목으로 공부한다는 뜻으로 '배우다'와 같이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Pairs with 배우다 to say you study it as a subject.

phrases.en: I borrowed a world history book from the library.
phrases.nuance_ko: '세계사' 뒤에 '책'을 붙여 읽을거리를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding 책 after it names a book on the topic.

explain_en: At school it is also the name of a subject taught separately from '한국사' (Korean history). That is why the two often appear together: '한국사와 세계사'.

examples.en: The deep forest is quiet and mysterious.
Even in photos, the aurora has a magical feel.
The stars in the night sky are shining mysteriously.

examples.ko: 그 호수가 왜 푸른지 신비하다고 생각했어요.
examples.en: I thought it was wondrous that the lake is so blue.
As a child, magic seemed truly mysterious.
I like stories that are both mysterious and scary.

explain: 설명하기 어려워서 놀랍고 끌리는 느낌에 써요. '이상하다'는 낯설고 어색해서 좋지 않을 수 있지만, '신비하다'는 보통 좋은 느낌이에요.

phrases.en: That lake has a mysterious atmosphere.
phrases.nuance_ko: '신비하다'와 같은 뜻이고, 뒤에 오는 말을 꾸밀 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means the same as 신비하다 and is often used before a noun.

phrases.example: 이 음악은 들으면 신비한 느낌이 들어요.
phrases.en: This music gives me a mysterious feeling.
phrases.nuance_ko: '신비하다'를 '-ㄴ' 꼴로 바꿔 '느낌'과 같이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The adjective changes to its -ㄴ form and goes with 느낌.

phrases.en: Under the moonlight the lake looks mysterious.
phrases.nuance_ko: 눈에 보이는 모습이 그렇다고 말할 때 '-아/어 보이다'를 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add -아/어 보이다 to say something looks that way.

explain_en: It describes something hard to explain that is amazing and attractive. '이상하다' can be negative, since it means strange or off, but '신비하다' usually carries a positive feeling.

p.n: The other word means it seems or feels mysterious.

examples.ko: 이 사진은 자연의 아름다움을 잘 보여 줘요.
examples.en: This photo shows the beauty of nature well.
I first came to know the beauty of song.
Beauty is different for each person.

examples.ko: 그 그림에서 겉모습보다 마음의 아름다움이 느껴졌어요.
examples.en: From that painting I felt the beauty of the heart more than looks.
We marveled at the beauty of the autumn mountains.

examples.ko: 아름다움을 찾는 눈이 있으면 일상이 달라져요.
examples.en: If you have an eye for beauty, daily life changes.

explain: 일상 대화에서는 '예뻐요', '멋있어요'가 훨씬 흔하고, 아름다움은 자연·예술·마음처럼 큰 대상을 말하는 글이나 연설에 어울려요. '아름답다'는 ㅂ불규칙이라 '아름다워요', '아름다운'으로 바뀌고, 명사는 '아름다움'이에요.

phrases.en: I saw beautiful scenery from the mountain.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 '아름다움'의 바탕이 되는 형용사로, 뒤에 명사가 오면 '아름다운'이 돼요.
phrases.nuance_en: The adjective behind '아름다움'; before a noun it becomes '아름다운'.

phrases.en: The autumn leaves are really beautiful.
phrases.nuance_ko: ㅂ불규칙이라 '아름답다'가 '아름다워요'로 바뀌어요. '예뻐요'보다 조금 격식 있고 글에 어울려요.
phrases.nuance_en: An irregular ㅂ adjective: '아름답다' becomes '아름다워요'. It sounds a bit more formal than '예뻐요' and suits writing.

phrases.example: 이 그림은 제 눈에는 아름답지 않아요.
phrases.en: This painting isn't beautiful to my eyes.
phrases.nuance_ko: '아름답다'의 부정형이에요. '제 눈에는'과 함께 쓰면 내 느낌을 조심스럽게 말할 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form of '아름답다'. Paired with '제 눈에는' it states your own opinion politely.

explain_en: In daily talk '예뻐요' and '멋있어요' are far more common; '아름다움' suits writing or speeches about big things like nature, art and the heart. The adjective '아름답다' is a ㅂ-irregular (아름다워요, 아름다운), and its noun form is '아름다움'.

examples.en: Anyway, we have to finish it today.
Anyway, I'm glad you arrived safely.
Anyway, let's meet once and talk.

examples.ko: 이유가 뭐든 어쨌건 약속은 지켜야 해요.
examples.en: Whatever the reason, you have to keep your promise anyway.
Anyway, I agree with this plan.
Anyway, the exam is over, so get some good rest.

explain: '어쨌든'과 뜻이 같아서 바꿔 쓸 수 있어요. 앞의 이야기는 접어 두고 중요한 결론이나 본론으로 돌아갈 때 써요. 문장 맨 앞에 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: Anyway, the exam is over, so let's rest.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뜻이 같고, 더 자주 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning and more commonly used.

phrases.en: Anyway, let's go home early today.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이야기를 정리하고 결론으로 갈 때 써요. 말할 때 자연스러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to wrap up and move to the point. Sounds natural in speech.

phrases.en: Regardless, you have to keep your promise.
phrases.nuance_ko: '간에'를 붙여서 '어떻든 상관없이'의 느낌을 더해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding 'gane' gives the feeling of 'regardless of how it is'.

explain_en: It has the same meaning as '어쨌든' and the two can be swapped. It is used to set aside what came before and return to the main point or conclusion. It often comes at the start of a sentence.

examples.en: Our class puts on a play at the festival.
The students performed a play on stage.
As a child I played with friends by acting out plays.
I saw a stage actor up close.
We'll be performing a play at the theater from tomorrow.
Don't put on an act and pretend to be sad.

explain: 무대 위 공연뿐 아니라 일부러 꾸며서 행동하는 것도 가리켜요. '연극하지 마'는 '진짜가 아닌 척하지 마'라는 느낌이라 친한 사이에서 써요. 공연 이야기에서는 '연극을 하다'처럼 목적어를 넣어 말하기도 해요.

phrases.en: We put on a play at school.
phrases.nuance_ko: '연극'을 목적어로 넣어 말해요. 공연 이야기에서 더 자주 들어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Here '연극' is the object. You hear this more often when talking about performances.

phrases.en: I said 'Stop acting' to my close friend.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일부러 꾸며서 행동하지 말라는 뜻이에요. 친한 사이에서만 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: It means don't put on a show. Use it only with close friends.

phrases.en: The actor plays a sad role on stage.
phrases.nuance_ko: 배우가 역할을 맡아 보여 주는 일이에요. 연극, 영화, 드라마에 두루 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: It means an actor playing a role. It works for plays, movies, and dramas.

explain_en: Besides stage performance, it can mean deliberately putting on an act. '연극하지 마' feels like 'stop pretending' and is said between close people. For a stage show you can also say '연극을 하다' with the object.

dis.h: put on a play; or fake an act

p.n: 연기하다 stresses acting a role; 연극하다 stresses putting on a play.

examples.ko: 할머니가 어릴 때 옛이야기를 많이 해 주셨어요.
examples.en: When I was little, my grandmother told me many old stories.
Interesting old tales are handed down in our village.

examples.ko: 옛이야기 속 호랑이는 무섭기도 하고 웃기기도 해요.
examples.en: The tiger in old tales is scary but also funny.
The class where we read foreign folk tales was fun.

examples.ko: 아이들이 잠들기 전에 옛이야기를 듣고 싶어 해요.
examples.en: The kids want to hear an old story before sleeping.

examples.ko: 이 책에는 옛이야기 열 편이 실려 있어요.
examples.en: This book contains ten old stories.

explain: '옛날이야기'와 같은 뜻인데 더 짧아서 글에서도 자주 보여요. 오래전부터 전해 내려오는 이야기에 잘 어울려요. 발음은 [옌니야기]로 'ㄴ' 소리가 덧나요.

phrases.en: Every evening I listened to my grandmother's old stories.
phrases.nuance_ko: '옛이야기'와 같은 뜻이고 말할 때 더 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as '옛이야기' and more common in speech.

phrases.en: Dad told the child an old story.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이야기를 해 줄 때 '들려주다'와 같이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used with '들려주다' when telling a story to someone.

phrases.en: I read an old tale together with my child.
phrases.nuance_ko: 책으로 옛이야기를 볼 때 '읽다'와 함께 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used with '읽다' when reading an old tale in a book.

explain_en: It means the same as '옛날이야기' but is shorter and common in writing too. It fits stories passed down from long ago. It is pronounced [옌니야기], with an added 'ㄴ' sound.

examples.en: I saw a unicorn in a storybook.
A unicorn has one horn on its forehead.
The child slept holding a unicorn doll.
A white unicorn flew through the sky.
The atmosphere was mysterious, like a unicorn.
A unicorn is drawn on this bag too.

explain: '용'이나 '봉황'처럼 실제로는 없는 상상 속 동물이에요. 사업 이야기에서는 비유로도 써서 '유니콘 기업'이라고 해요.

phrases.example: 그 회사는 곧 유니콘 기업이 될 거예요.
phrases.en: unicorn company
phrases.nuance_ko: 짧은 기간에 아주 크게 성장한 새 회사를 가리켜요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to a young company that has grown very large in a short time.

explain_en: Like 용 and 봉황, it is an imaginary animal that does not really exist. In business talk it is also used as a metaphor in the phrase 유니콘 기업.

examples.en: The two people's opinions match.
The name doesn't match the document.
Our hobbies matched, so we became close quickly.
I like people whose words and actions match.
If our times match, let's go together.
The police said the fingerprints matched.

explain: '일치하다'는 '~와/과 일치하다'처럼 비교하는 두 대상이 둘 다 필요해요. 주어가 '둘'이면 '의견이 일치하다'처럼 쓸 수도 있어요. 반대말은 '다르다', '일치하지 않다'예요.

phrases.en: My answer exactly matches the correct answer.
phrases.nuance_ko: '정확히'를 붙여 완전히 같다고 강조해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding 정확히 stresses that the two match completely.

phrases.en: We are looking for a person who matches the conditions.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뒤의 명사를 꾸며서 '맞는'이라는 뜻으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Modifies the noun after it, meaning 'matching'.

phrases.en: My idea is the same as my senior's idea.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상 대화에서 더 쉽게 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A simpler word for everyday conversation.

explain_en: 일치하다 needs two things being compared, as in '~와/과 일치하다'. If the subject itself is plural, as in 의견이 일치하다, no second noun is needed. The opposite is 다르다 or 일치하지 않다.

examples.en: The market in our neighborhood is a big source of pride.

examples.ko: 자랑거리는 많은데 겸손해서 말을 안 해요.
examples.en: He has plenty to boast about but is modest and doesn't say it.
The only thing I can be proud of is being diligent.

examples.ko: 이 상은 우리 가족의 자랑거리로 남을 거예요.
examples.en: This award will remain a source of pride for our family.
Tell us your achievements to be proud of, one by one.

examples.ko: 남에게 보여 줄 만한 자랑거리가 생겼어요.
examples.en: I now have something worth showing off to others.

explain: '자랑하다'는 행동이고 '자랑거리'는 자랑할 대상이에요. 사람이 느끼는 마음은 '자랑스럽다'로 말해요. '이야깃거리', '걱정거리'처럼 '-거리'가 붙은 말이 많아요.

phrases.example: 이 상은 우리 가족의 자랑거리가 됐어요.
phrases.en: This award became something to be proud of for our family.
phrases.nuance_ko: 자랑할 만한 일이 생겼을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when something worth boasting about arises.
phrases.en_equiv: become something to be proud of

phrases.en: Our school has a lot to be proud of.
phrases.nuance_ko: 자랑할 것이 여러 가지라는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means there are many things to be proud of.
phrases.en_equiv: have a lot to be proud of

phrases.en: I'm really proud of my son.
phrases.nuance_ko: 자랑거리를 보고 느끼는 마음을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The feeling you have toward something you're proud of.

explain_en: '자랑하다' is the act of boasting, while '자랑거리' is the thing to boast about. The feeling a person has is '자랑스럽다'. Many words take '-거리', like '이야깃거리' and '걱정거리'.

examples.ko: 끝없는 들판 너머로 지평선이 펼쳐져 있어요.
examples.en: The horizon stretches out beyond the endless fields.

examples.ko: 저녁이 되자 지평선 너머로 해가 졌어요.
examples.en: When evening came, the sun set beyond the horizon.

examples.ko: 산이 없는 넓은 평야에서는 지평선이 잘 보여요.
examples.en: On a wide plain without mountains you can see the horizon well.
The road continues far away to the horizon.

examples.ko: 하늘 아래 지평선에 붉은 노을이 번졌어요.
examples.en: Red sunset glow spread across the horizon under the sky.

examples.ko: 차를 타고 가도 지평선이 가까워지지 않아요.
examples.en: Even riding in a car, the horizon does not get any closer.

explain: 바다 끝에 보이는 선은 '수평선', 땅 끝에 보이는 선은 지평선이라고 구분해요. 한국은 산이 많아서 지평선을 보기 어렵고, 김제 같은 넓은 평야에서 볼 수 있다고들 해요.

phrases.en: You can see the horizon from here.
phrases.nuance_ko: 넓은 땅 끝의 선이 눈에 들어올 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when the line at the edge of the land comes into view.

phrases.en: Rice fields continue to the horizon.
phrases.nuance_ko: '까지'를 붙여 아주 멀리까지 넓다는 느낌을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: With 까지 it gives a sense of reaching far into the distance.
phrases.en_equiv: all the way to the horizon

phrases.en: You can see the horizon over the sea.
phrases.nuance_ko: 바다 끝의 선은 '수평선'이라고 해서 지평선과 구분해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The line at the sea's edge is 수평선, unlike 지평선 for land.

explain_en: The line at the end of the sea is '수평선', and the line at the end of land is 지평선. Korea has many mountains, so a horizon is hard to see; people say you can see it on wide plains like Gimje.

en: to be honest; to be sincere

examples.en: That friend's words are sincere.
I felt better after receiving a sincere apology.
His eyes looked sincere.

examples.ko: 진실하게 말하면 모두가 이해해 줄 거예요.
examples.en: If you speak honestly, everyone will understand.
You quickly notice compliments that are not sincere.

examples.ko: 진실하고 따뜻한 친구는 힘들 때 곁에 있어요.
examples.en: A sincere and warm friend stays by your side in hard times.

explain: '솔직하다'는 숨기지 않고 말한다는 느낌이고, '진실하다'는 마음과 말에 거짓이 없다는 느낌이에요. 사람의 성격에 써요. 사실을 말하는 명사 '진실'과 같은 뿌리의 말이에요.

phrases.en: I can feel his sincere heart.
phrases.nuance_ko: 거짓 없는 마음을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to a heart with no falseness.

phrases.en: What he says is not honest.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-지 않다'로 말이나 행동에 거짓이 있다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Says that words or actions are not truthful.

phrases.en: That friend really looks sincere.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-아/어 보이다'로 겉모습에서 받은 느낌을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: '-아/어 보이다' expresses an impression from appearance.

explain_en: '솔직하다' feels like speaking without hiding anything, while '진실하다' feels like having no falseness in heart and words. It describes a person's character. It shares a root with the noun '진실', meaning the truth.

examples.en: You can see kangaroos in Australia.
At the zoo I saw a kangaroo hopping.
We lined up to see the baby kangaroo.
I want to jump high like a kangaroo.
I gave a kangaroo doll to my younger sibling as a present.
I put up pictures of a kangaroo and a koala on the wall.

explain: 동물 이름이지만 '캥거루족'이라는 말로도 들려요. 어른이 되어서도 부모와 함께 살며 도움을 받는 사람을 가리켜요.

phrases.example: 서른이 넘어도 부모님 집에 사는 캥거루족이 늘고 있어요.
phrases.en: adult who keeps living off their parents
phrases.nuance_ko: 어른이 되어서도 부모에게 기대어 사는 사람을 가리켜요. 놀리는 느낌이 있어서 다른 사람에게 쓸 때는 조심해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to adults who keep living with and relying on their parents. It has a teasing tone, so be careful using it about others.

explain_en: It is an animal name, but you also hear it in '캥거루족', which refers to adults who keep living with and relying on their parents.

examples.en: This small island is a paradise for travelers.
We rested on a beach like paradise.

examples.ko: 책이 가득한 도서관은 제게 파라다이스처럼 느껴져요.
examples.en: A library full of books feels like paradise to me.

examples.ko: 파라다이스라는 이름의 작은 가게에서 빵을 샀어요.
examples.en: I bought bread at a small shop named Paradise.
I felt at ease as if I had come to paradise.
A place like this is paradise itself.

explain: 비슷한 말로 한자어 '낙원'이 있어요. 외래어 파라다이스는 휴양지나 가게 이름에, 비유로 '○○의 파라다이스'라고 쓸 때도 있어요. '지상 낙원'처럼 굳은 말은 '낙원'을 써요.

phrases.en: This park is a paradise for children.
phrases.nuance_ko: '파라다이스'와 같은 뜻의 한자어로, 글이나 일반 대화에서 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The Sino-Korean word with the same meaning, used in writing and general talk.

phrases.en: That island is like heaven on earth.
phrases.nuance_ko: 굳어진 말이라 '낙원'을 써서 표현해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A fixed expression that uses 낙원.

phrases.en: This street is a shopping paradise.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어떤 활동을 하기에 아주 좋은 곳을 비유로 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A figurative way to call a place perfect for some activity.

explain_en: A similar Chinese-origin word is '낙원'. The loanword 'paradaiseu' appears in resort or shop names, and also figuratively, as in '○○의 파라다이스'. Fixed phrases such as '지상 낙원' use '낙원'.
